name: Seattle-Tacoma Box Co
old_description: Founded by a six-generation packaging company in 1991, SeaCa Packaging expanded the family legacy of reliable service, commitment to deliveries and customer focused approach by providing high quality graphic packaging to Central California.
about:
Seattle-Tacoma Box Company has operated from Kent, Washington since 1889, making it one of the oldest continuously family-owned packaging firms in the Pacific Northwest. The business traces its roots through six generations of the founding family, who have maintained ownership and operational control since the late 19th century. In 1991 the family expanded its footprint by launching SeaCa Packaging to serve Central California with graphic packaging, and in 2014 added SeaCa Plastic Packaging for sustainable polypropylene corrugated products. A sister operation, Commencement Bay Corrugated, was established in the early 1980s as an independent corrugated plant jointly owned by the presidents of Seattle-Tacoma Box Company and Pacific Container Company.

The company manufactures a full range of corrugated, plastic, and wooden packaging at dedicated wood and corrugated plants. Capabilities include custom structural design, printing, and die-cutting for produce bins, shipping containers, and retail-ready packaging. While specific facility dimensions and headcount are not disclosed, the combined operations serve high-volume agricultural harvest cycles across the region.

Primary customers are growers, packers, and shippers in the fruit, vegetable, and seafood sectors throughout Washington, Oregon, and California. The packaging is engineered for cold-chain durability, ventilation, and brand presentation, with documented use cases in apple, berry, and salmon supply chains.

The firm emphasizes its multi-generational expertise and a sustainability platform built on certified forest content, certified sourcing, and recycled materials. The family ownership model is cited as the foundation for long-term customer relationships and consistent service through seasonal demand spikes.
